podcast.title: Barbecue Band (2004)
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance served as a "Barbecue Band" on the Warped Tour in 2004, meaning they cooked post-show dinner for the performers and crew in exchange for being able to play on the tour themselves. While fulfilling this duty, they were also playing new songs. "They were the Barbecue Band in 2004."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup (2013)
podcast.body: The band's breakup in 2013 contributed to the decline in popularity of the emo and pop punk genres. "The fact that my chemical romance broke up in 2013 did not help."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: 2020 Reunion and Tour Success
podcast.body: The band reunited in 2020, following a period where many emo bands had broken up. Their subsequent North American tour experienced immense demand, selling out completely in less than two hours. "And in 2020, my chemical romance reunited. Their entire North American tour sold out in less than two hours."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Gerard Way "Transformed Into a Demon" TikTok Theory (2025 Reunion Tour)
podcast.body: During My Chemical Romance's 2025 reunion tour, a TikTok user claimed that vocalist Gerard Way "transformed into a demon" mid-performance, generating a viral conspiracy theory among fans. "A TikTok user claimed that vocalist Gerard Way 'transformed into a demon' mid-performance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 40 or so Minutes (2025 Edition)

podcast.title: Added Twist to Emo
podcast.body: As emo music gained mainstream popularity, My Chemical Romance was noted for adding a "new twist to things," contributing to the evolution and continued momentum of the genre within the broader alternative music landscape. "Groups like Mike Chemical Romance added a new twist to things."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Comic Book Artist and Creator
podcast.body: Gerard Way began his journey in comic books at the age of 16, with his first comic, "On Raven's Wings," having two issues published. By 2001, he was interning as a sketch artist at Cartoon Network in New York, where he pitched an animated TV series called "The Breakfast Monkey," though it was not picked up. The experience of living through 9/11 profoundly impacted him, prompting him to leave animation to pursue music, which led to the formation of My Chemical Romance. In 2007, he began work on the mini-series "The Umbrella Academy," which became a significant success and was later adapted into a popular Netflix series. He also worked with the Marvel Universe on Spider-Man, creating the character of Penny Parker. "It was Gerard Way that created the character of Penny Parker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contemporary Concept Album Artists
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance is mentioned as one of the contemporary acts currently releasing concept albums. "Hello again, I'm Ellie Cross and with all the concept albums that we're seeing these days, Nine Inch Nails, My Chemical Romance, Coheating Cambria, The Arcade Fire, 30 Seconds to Mars, I thought it might be cool if we went back through the history of Alt Rock to see where all this came from."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early 2000s Emo Peak and Late 2010s Return
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance was a prominent band during Emo's peak in the early 2000s. They "disappeared" by the early 2010s as the genre waned, but returned by the end of the decade, signaling a strong emo revival alongside a new generation of groups exploring the genre. "It had its moments early in the century with bands like Dashboard Conventional and saves the day, Thursday, store the year, taking back Sunday and my chemical romance." "My chemical romance disappeared." "By the end of the decade, my chemical romance was back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Emo Trend Leader
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance was identified as a key band in the emo trend that emerged and peaked in the first decade of the 21st century, and they are also credited with leading the emo revival in the 2020s. "That was part of the emo trend that built and peaked in the first decade of the 21st century. And they're also the band leading the emo revival of the 2020s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Goth Leanings
podcast.body: This band, categorized as "emo-ish," emphasizes Goth leanings, particularly through their visual style. "Some emo-ish bands emphasize their Goth leanings, especially with their look. Check out 30 seconds to Mars or my chemical romance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Largest Emo Band
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance was identified as arguably the biggest band within the Emo movement. Their prominence marked the peak of Emo's popularity, an alt-rock trend known for burning "very hot and very bright" before its decline around 2009. "Perhaps the biggest band of them all was this group by Chemical Romance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15

podcast.title: Legacy of Mid-90s Punk Revival
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance is one of the bands whose existence can be directly attributed to the impact of the mid-1990s punk rock revival. "It's certainly not a stretch to say the groups like... My Chemical Romance, and many others wouldn't have existed had it not been for what happened in the middle 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Cure Influence
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance was cited as a group influenced by The Cure, demonstrating the breadth of The Cure's impact on bands across various subgenres of alternative music. "if you're looking for bands influenced by them we can turn to groups like Interpol, Smashing Pumpkins, The Killers, Nine-H Nails, My Chemical Romance, and so many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reunion for Touring
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance was one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

podcast.title: Soundfont Versions Popularity
podcast.body: My Chemical Romance is listed as one of the bands whose song versions contributed to the popularization of the soundfont genre in 2022, attracting significant viewership and listens online. "Versiones de canciones de Nirvana, Pixies, Rhyde Head, Michael Romance, empezaron a acumular miles y miles de views."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: El fenómeno de Soundfont Album. Discos reinterpretados en videojuegos

podcast.title: Theatrical Live Performances
podcast.body: In concert, My Chemical Romance adopted a highly theatrical approach for *The Black Parade*, featuring extensive role-playing and costumes, which was also reflected in the music video for "Welcome to the Black Parade." "In concert, my chemical romance was very theatrical about all this, lots of role playing in costumes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

concerts.title: 2025 Reunion Tour
concerts.body: My Chemical Romance has a reunion tour scheduled for 2025, which includes performances in stadiums. "My chemical romance has a 2025 reunion tour planned. Stadiums."

xref.body: The Misfits have been cited as influences by a diverse array of bands including Metallica, The Offspring, Green Day, My Chemical Romance, Guns N' Roses, Foo Fighters, and AFI. "Here is a short list of bands who say that they were influenced by the Missfits. Metallica, the offspring, Green Day, by chemical romance, guns and roses, Foo Fighters, AFI."

xref.title: Ongoing Touring Presence
xref.body: The Cure continues to tour today, maintaining their legacy and connection with fans, a testament to their enduring influence in rock music. "The Cure continues to tour today, and if you're looking for bands influenced by them we can turn to groups like Interpol, Smashing Pumpkins, The Killers, Nine-H Nails, My Chemical Romance, and so many more."
